title: Conga (tall barrel drums)
summary: The conga is a tall barrel drum of Afro-Cuban music, played in sets of two to four drums, quinto, conga and tumba, from the highest to the deepest. Each is struck with the fingers and the palm for open tones, slaps and muffled strokes.
howToPlay: Three drums stand in a row: the high quinto on the left, the middle conga and the deep tumba on the right.
On each drum the centre gives an open tone and the outer ring a sharp slap.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the steady tumbao, then add the slaps.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar, played in eighth notes.
heritageNote: In Cuban rumba and son the conga drums share one rhythm between them. The quinto improvises on top while the conga and tumba keep the tumbao, the steady pattern the dancers step to.
credits: Tradition: the conga drums; patterns written for this game
